How To Read This

<<<<<<< HEAD

reflex-quant has the strongest relative profile in this run, 21.4% ahead of alien-signals by geometric mean. It takes 31 of 51 scenarios decisively, while alien-signals takes 5.

Each scenario was measured with all frameworks on one VM. The row interval is a 95% order-statistic interval for the median within one process: it covers sample noise only, not a new process, another VM or another CPU model. The leaderboard score has no interval of its own: it was measured on one VM per scenario, and different scenarios ran on different CPU models. A ≈ next to a time means its interval overlaps the leader's; such scenarios count as nobody's win. Capped rows use one cold sample and have no interval. All intervals describe repeat measurements of this run on GitHub-hosted runners, not the speed of a runtime on other hardware. Hover a row for its interval and noise.

Interpret wins through the scenario taxonomy: creation, update, pull/push propagation, dynamic dependency churn, large graphs, lifecycle pressure, and memory behavior can favor different runtimes.

=======

reflex-quant has the strongest relative profile in this run, 24.7% ahead of reflex by geometric mean. It takes 8 of 51 scenarios decisively, while reflex takes 0.

Each scenario was measured with all frameworks on one VM, on 3 independent VM sets, in 3 fresh processes per VM. The row score is the median of the per-machine estimates and its interval is their range; with 3 machines a range covers the cross-machine median with only ~75% probability, so it is not a 95% interval. The leaderboard score is computed separately for each of the 3 machine sets (ratios within one VM) and the median is shown with the range; a ≈ next to a rank means its range overlaps the one above. A ≈ next to a time means its interval overlaps the leader's; such scenarios count as nobody's win. Capped rows use one cold sample and have no interval. All intervals describe repeat measurements of this run on GitHub-hosted runners, not the speed of a runtime on other hardware. Hover a row for its interval and noise.

Interpret wins through the scenario taxonomy: creation, update, pull/push propagation, dynamic dependency churn, large graphs, lifecycle pressure, and memory behavior can favor different runtimes.

Not ranked: @reatom/core (11 failed: out-of-memory, timeout); dalien-signals (1 failed: stack-overflow); kairo 0.8 alpha (11 failed: timeout); Svelte v5 (9 failed: timeout). A failed row (wrong result, crash, out of memory, timeout) is a result; scoring such a library over only the scenarios it completed would rank it on an easier workload set. Its completed rows still appear in every per-test card.

Where The Noise Is

Spread of a row's medianTypical (median row)Rows
within one process±1.5%1387
between fresh processes±3.0%1387
between machines±19.5%1387

Each level is the standard deviation of ln(time), shown as an approximate relative spread, and includes the noise of the levels listed above it. The machine level compares per-machine estimates that are already medians over fresh processes, so it can be smaller than the process level. A within-process 95% interval only covers sample noise; in this run a fresh process or another machine typically moves a row 12.9x as much. Only the machine-level range reflects all three.
